Trajectory, Pseudotime, and Dynamic Genes

Source: vignettes/trajectory-dynamics.Rmd
trajectory-dynamics.Rmd

Shennong uses Slingshot as the default cluster-aware trajectory backend and tradeSeq for negative-binomial smooth models. The workflow stores a versioned result instead of only adding a single pseudotime vector to cell metadata.

This article reads the locally materialized Hermann mouse spermatogenesis fixture from SHENNONG_REAL_DATA_DIR. The analysis runs only when that file is present and SHENNONG_RUN_VIGNETTES=true; a normal package check therefore knits the article without downloading data or executing the analysis.

data.frame(
  step = c("fixture and clustering", "Slingshot + tradeSeq trajectory"),
  status = c(
    if (run_vignette) "executed below" else "disabled or fixture missing",
    if (trajectory_ready) "executed below" else "extended profile or optional dependencies unavailable"
  )
)

Load and prepare the real trajectory fixture

The fixture retains total counts plus the original spliced and unspliced layers. We remove only cells whose source annotation is missing, then use Shennong’s standard clustering workflow to create the PCA and UMAP reductions needed by downstream trajectory plots.

library(Shennong)
library(dplyr)

trajectory_object <- qs2::qs_read(trajectory_fixture)
annotated <- !is.na(trajectory_object$real_cell_type) &
  nzchar(as.character(trajectory_object$real_cell_type))
trajectory_object <- subset(
  trajectory_object,
  cells = colnames(trajectory_object)[annotated]
)

tibble::tibble(
  fixture_file = basename(trajectory_fixture),
  cells = ncol(trajectory_object),
  features = nrow(trajectory_object),
  layers = paste(SeuratObject::Layers(trajectory_object[["RNA"]]), collapse = ", ")
)

sort(table(trajectory_object$real_cell_type), decreasing = TRUE)

trajectory_object <- sn_run_cluster(
  object = trajectory_object,
  normalization_method = "seurat",
  nfeatures = min(1500L, nrow(trajectory_object)),
  npcs = 30,
  dims = 1:20,
  resolution = 0.6,
  cluster_algorithm = "louvain",
  cluster_name = "trajectory_cluster",
  species = "mouse",
  verbose = FALSE
)

sn_plot_dim(
  trajectory_object,
  reduction = "umap",
  group_by = "real_cell_type",
  title = "Hermann spermatogenesis cell types"
)

Infer and store the extended trajectory

Trajectory orientation is not inferred from the embedding. The code resolves an early spermatogonial label and a late spermatid label from the source annotations, then maps each biological anchor to its dominant unsupervised cluster. This preserves the real source labels as endpoint evidence while avoiding unstable lineage geometry from very small source-label groups. If either anchor cannot be resolved, the article stops rather than guessing an orientation.

first_matching_label <- function(labels, patterns, role) {
  for (pattern in patterns) {
    hit <- labels[grepl(pattern, labels, ignore.case = TRUE)]
    if (length(hit)) return(hit[[1]])
  }
  stop(
    "Could not resolve the ", role, " trajectory label from: ",
    paste(labels, collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

source_labels <- sort(unique(as.character(trajectory_object$real_cell_type)))
start_label <- first_matching_label(
  source_labels,
  c("spermatogon", "undifferentiated", "^spg", "stem"),
  "start"
)
end_label <- first_matching_label(
  source_labels,
  c(
    "late.*round.*spermatid", "elongat.*spermatid",
    "round.*spermatid", "spermatid", "^spt"
  ),
  "end"
)
if (identical(start_label, end_label)) {
  stop("Resolved trajectory start and end labels are identical.", call. = FALSE)
}

dominant_cluster <- function(source_label) {
  members <- as.character(trajectory_object$real_cell_type) == source_label
  counts <- sort(
    table(as.character(trajectory_object$trajectory_cluster[members])),
    decreasing = TRUE
  )
  if (!length(counts)) {
    stop("No unsupervised cluster represents source label `", source_label, "`.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  names(counts)[[1]]
}

start_cluster <- dominant_cluster(start_label)
end_cluster <- dominant_cluster(end_label)
if (identical(start_cluster, end_cluster)) {
  stop(
    "Biological trajectory endpoints map to the same unsupervised cluster `",
    start_cluster, "`.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

counts <- SeuratObject::LayerData(
  trajectory_object,
  assay = "RNA",
  layer = "counts"
)
detected_cells <- Matrix::rowSums(counts > 0)
stable_hvgs <- SeuratObject::VariableFeatures(trajectory_object)
stable_hvgs <- stable_hvgs[detected_cells[stable_hvgs] >= 50L]
dynamic_features <- utils::head(stable_hvgs, 10L)
if (length(dynamic_features) < 4L) {
  stop(
    "Fewer than four variable genes are detected in at least 50 real cells.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}
trend_features <- utils::head(dynamic_features, 4L)

tibble::tibble(
  endpoint = c("start", "end"),
  source_label = c(start_label, end_label),
  dominant_cluster = c(start_cluster, end_cluster),
  dynamic_features = length(dynamic_features)
)

trajectory_object <- sn_run_trajectory(
  trajectory_object,
  method = "slingshot",
  reduction = "pca",
  cluster_by = "trajectory_cluster",
  start = start_cluster,
  end = end_cluster,
  result_id = "spermatogenesis",
  dynamic_features = dynamic_features,
  max_dynamic_features = length(dynamic_features),
  nknots = 3L,
  trend_features = trend_features,
  trend_points = 40L,
  seed = 717L
)

Inspect the retained evidence

The cell table retains pseudotime and lineage probability for every inferred lineage. Dynamic-gene, fitted-trend, convergence, and terminal-state tables are kept with the topology rather than recomputed inside plotting code.

sn_list_results(trajectory_object, type = "trajectory")

trajectory <- sn_get_result(
  trajectory_object,
  type = "trajectory",
  result_id = "spermatogenesis"
)

head(trajectory$tables$cells)
trajectory$tables$terminal_states
trajectory$graphs$lineages
trajectory$diagnostics

trajectory$tables$dynamic_genes |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$adjusted_p_value) |>
  head(10L)

trajectory$tables$convergence |>
  head(10L)

Backend output is accepted only when cell identities and lineage dimensions align. Every positive lineage weight must have a finite pseudotime. For a multi-lineage result, explicit weights are required; primary_lineage is the maximum valid weight, and cells with no positive eligible weight retain NA rather than being assigned arbitrarily to the first lineage. Formal tradeSeq fitting reads counts_layer and requires finite, non-negative integer raw or corrected counts—normalized expression is not rounded into counts.

Plot topology, pseudotime, and gene dynamics

The lineage name is taken from the stored graph, so the probability plot stays aligned with the backend result instead of assuming a hard-coded name.

lineage_name <- names(trajectory$graphs$lineages)[[1]]

sn_plot_trajectory(trajectory)
sn_plot_pseudotime(trajectory, lineage = lineage_name)
sn_plot_lineage_probability(trajectory, lineage = lineage_name)
sn_plot_dynamic_heatmap(trajectory)
sn_plot_gene_trend(trajectory, features = trend_features)
sn_plot_branch_comparison(trajectory, test = "pattern")

Extended backends are explicit

The all profile may run Monocle 3 only when its R dependency is already installed. The article does not install packages while knitting. The direct Monocle 3 path uses a real umap reduction by default and will not relabel PCA coordinates as UMAP. It also fails on an end constraint or multiple disconnected partitions that cannot be represented faithfully by this adapter; use an explicit external result/runner when those semantics are required.

tibble::tibble(
  backend = c("monocle3", "palantir"),
  profile_all = run_extended,
  dependency_or_result_available = c(
    requireNamespace("monocle3", quietly = TRUE),
    nzchar(palantir_result_path) && file.exists(palantir_result_path)
  ),
  will_run = c(run_monocle3, run_palantir)
)
monocle <- sn_run_trajectory(
  trajectory_object,
  method = "monocle3",
  reduction = "umap",
  cluster_by = "real_cell_type",
  start = start_label,
  test_dynamic = FALSE,
  seed = 717L,
  return_object = FALSE
)

head(monocle$tables$cells)
sn_plot_pseudotime(monocle)

Palantir is an explicit adapter boundary. It runs only when the all profile is active and SHENNONG_PALANTIR_RESULT points to a real, named per-cell result serialized with qs2; this article never fabricates adapter output.

palantir_result <- qs2::qs_read(palantir_result_path)
palantir <- sn_run_trajectory(
  trajectory_object,
  method = "palantir",
  reduction = "pca",
  cluster_by = "real_cell_type",
  start = start_label,
  end = end_label,
  test_dynamic = FALSE,
  backend_control = list(result = palantir_result),
  return_object = FALSE
)

sn_validate_result(palantir)
head(palantir$tables$cells)
sn_plot_trajectory(palantir)
